tasks.title: Create the cargo workspace and wire the rust gates, with versions pinned from the tech radar
tasks.proof: `just gate` now runs the rust-gate recipe instead of skipping it, and every step passes: cargo fmt --all --check clean, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean, 48 nextest tests passed, 6 doctests passed. Verified 2026-08-03. Scope note: downpour-http and downpour-cli are created by S1-T7 and S1-T12, the tasks that give them content, rather than as empty placeholders here; `members = ["crates/*"]` picks them up with no workspace edit.

tasks.title: downpour-types: RemoteObject and a RangeSupport whose Proven variant cannot be constructed without a validated 206
tasks.proof: crates/downpour-types/tests/range_proof.rs (12 tests) — RangeSupport::Proven is reachable only through RangeProof::from_observed_response, whose 12 negative cases cover 200-instead-of-206, 416, absent Content-Range, malformed Content-Range, mismatched Content-Range, gzip-on-range, unknown total length, and a full body behind a 206. Plus crates/downpour-types/tests/validator.rs (10 tests) for validator classification and digest capture. Verified red-before-green: deleting the Content-Encoding check makes a_gzipped_range_response_is_rejected fail.

tasks.title: Strict Content-Range parser that validates the response against the range that was actually requested
tasks.proof: crates/downpour-types/tests/content_range_prop.rs::never_accepts_a_range_inconsistent_with_the_request — proptest over arbitrary requested/returned range pairs asserting consistency iff the start matches exactly and the end is within the request; plus parsing_never_panics, parsing_preserves_the_range, and a 15-case malformed-header table from RFC 9110 section 14.4. Verified red-before-green: deleting the start-offset check makes the property and a_short_but_aligned_range_is_consistent both fail.

tasks.title: Filename resolution (Content-Disposition RFC 6266 including filename*, URL-path fallback) and sanitisation
tasks.proof: crates/downpour-types/tests/filename_prop.rs::sanitised_name_is_always_exactly_one_normal_component — proptest over arbitrary char sequences asserting the result is one Component::Normal, non-empty, at most 255 bytes, and free of separators and control characters; plus sanitise_is_idempotent, resolve_never_panics, and a 22-case table covering ../, absolute paths, Windows-style paths, NUL, control characters, the Windows reserved device names, trailing dots and spaces, and multibyte truncation.

tasks.title: ADR-0010: the corpus case format and the pathology-server contract
tasks.proof: docs/adr/0010-corpus-case-format.md exists with a Reversal trigger section naming three specific, measurable signals; registered in the docs/adr/README.md index and in adr_index here. Status is `proposed`, not `accepted`: .claude/skills/adr-new/SKILL.md step 5 reserves acceptance for the maintainer, so an agent marking its own ADR accepted would defeat the point. scripts/check-links.sh resolves the new links.

tasks.title: Pathology server: deterministic PRNG content, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, and the ranges/framing/redirects behaviours
tasks.proof: tests/corpus/tests/content_generator.rs (12 tests): the construction is pinned against an independent reimplementation of the ADR-0010 spec, anchored to the published BLAKE3 empty-input test vector, and asserted to have no zero runs (a hole would hide in one) and entropy > 7.99 bits/byte (a gzipped body could pass for a plausible length in compressible content). first_mismatch reports an exact absolute offset, verified against an injected 4 KiB hole. STILL OUTSTANDING for this task: the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 servers and the ranges/framing/redirects behaviours.
tasks.notes: Content generator DONE and committed. Server NOT started. Next concrete step: hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 server over tokio TcpListener (hand-rolled because pathologies like a wrong Content-Length, no length and no chunked framing, and a mid-body close cannot be expressed through a conforming HTTP library), then HTTP/2 via hyper over cleartext h2c. Decision to record when the server lands: the corpus uses plaintext h1 and h2c rather than TLS, because docs/09 section 7 requires local offline tests and TLS would add certificate management for no S1 coverage gain; ALPN negotiation belongs to the protocols category in S5.

risks.text: Scope sprawl: the project fails by growing sideways rather than by being technically hard
risks.mitigation: Stage gates as hard walls; backlog instead of implementation; non-goals listed explicitly in docs/00

risks.text: Silent corruption ships undetected because it is invisible in casual testing
risks.mitigation: Deterministic content generator gives ground truth per byte; crash injection at every write boundary; scorecard row 1 is a release blocker

risks.text: The Rust HTTP/3 stack stays experimental and cannot be shipped
risks.mitigation: TransferProtocol trait keeps h3 quarantined behind a feature flag; S6 may legitimately end with 'works, stays behind the flag'

risks.text: Browser extension store review rejects or delays the extension over native messaging and host permissions
risks.mitigation: Minimal permissions with written justification; no remote code; reproducible build from source; version skew handled by the IPC handshake

risks.text: Single-maintainer bandwidth: ten stages is a long road
risks.mitigation: Each stage produces something independently useful; the CLI is a shippable product from S3 onward

risks.text: AI agents produce plausible code that does not compose into a system
risks.mitigation: The harness: PROVE-before-BUILD, Gate A proof fields, Gate D corpus rule, machine-validated progress file

risks.text: The compatibility corpus is not maintained and the strategy quietly fails
risks.mitigation: Gate D is non-waivable: no fix lands without its case; corpus metrics tracked in this file

risks.text: Adaptive concurrency oscillates or underperforms a well-chosen fixed count
risks.mitigation: Dedicated simulation scenarios; ADR-0009 names the fallback (fixed count with learned per-origin defaults)

backlog.text: downpour-cli links downpour-http directly in S1 because no daemon exists yet. When downpour-daemon lands, move the transfer behind IPC so the architecture rule 'clients never link the engine' (docs/02 section 3) holds again.
backlog.rationale: Roadmap S1 lists only three crates, so a direct link is the only option now; recorded so it is not mistaken for the intended end state

backlog.text: The minimal file sink written in S1 (crates/downpour-http/src/sink.rs) is superseded by downpour-storage in S2, which owns preallocation, positional writes, the journal and the durability ordering (I-1, I-9, I-10).
backlog.rationale: S1-C6 needs verify-before-rename now, but S1 has no storage crate to put it in

backlog.text: S1 captures a server-supplied Repr-Digest/Content-Digest but does not verify it. S2 must verify a captured digest before the final rename (I-4), which needs base64 decoding and sha2. Until then, no S1 corpus case may supply a digest, or the engine would be ignoring evidence it holds.
backlog.rationale: docs/03 section 2.1 step 6 says record it; I-4 says check it when the server supplied one. S1 does the first half only, deliberately.

backlog.text: RangeProof deliberately does not derive Deserialize: a derived impl would be a second constructor that skips the validation, turning the compiler-enforced I-6 back into a convention. When S2 persists a RemoteObject it must either re-validate on load or store the raw observation and rebuild the proof from it.
backlog.rationale: The hazard is invisible at the point where someone will reach for #[derive(Deserialize)], so it is recorded rather than left to be rediscovered

Two S1 tasks have no blocker and can start immediately — S1-T1 (workspace) and S1-T5 (ADR-0010, the corpus case format, which must be written before the pathology server in S1-T6). session_log.summary: S1-T1 through S1-T4: cargo workspace (resolver 3, edition 2024, MSRV 1.97.1) with the tech-radar pins re-verified against crates.io, nextest profiles, and workspace lints that encode .claude/rules/rust.md mechanically. downpour-types implements the pure half of the probe: a strict Content-Range parser validated against the requested range, filename resolution and sanitisation, validator classification, and digest capture. I-6 is enforced structurally rather than by discipline: RangeSupport::Proven carries a RangeProof whose fields are private and whose single constructor returns Err unless the response validated, so no expression in the workspace can produce Proven without the evidence. 48 tests and 6 doctests pass; fmt and clippy -D warnings clean.
session_log.left_in_progress: S1-T5 (ADR-0010, the corpus case format) is next and unblocks S1-T6, the pathology server. S1-T7 (TransferProtocol trait + h1h2 backend) can proceed in parallel; it only needed downpour-types, which is now done. Branch: feature/s1-foundations.
